canonical_statement: For a classical solution of the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on R^3 with sufficiently regular divergence-free initial velocity, failure to continue at a finite maximal time T forces the time integral on [0,T) of the spatial L-infinity norm of the vorticity curl u to diverge; equivalently, finiteness of that integral is a continuation criterion.
domain_and_universes: Time interval [0,T), space R^3, velocity u(t,x) in a classical/Sobolev solution class; precise Lean universes and analytic structures remain open
quantifiers: divergence-free initial velocity u0 of sufficient Sobolev regularity
u, p forming the corresponding classical incompressible Euler solution on [0,T) x R^3
hypotheses: partial_t u + (u dot nabla) u = -nabla p
T is a finite maximal existence time for the noncontinuation direction
conclusion: Integral from 0 to T of ||curl u(t)||_(L-infinity(R^3)) dt is infinite; contrapositively, a finite integral permits continuation beyond T

alternate_encodings.relationship: related variant, not identified with the R^3 root
expected consequence/equivalent criterion under a local well-posedness theorem

excluded_degenerate_cases: Two-dimensional Euler, Navier-Stokes, bounded domains, periodic domains, weak solutions, and one-sided estimates without a continuation theorem are outside the frozen root unless later connected by checked transports.
